name: Ochanomizu
tagline: Otemachi in 4 minutes and Tokyo in 5 minutes. Served by 4 lines.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, served by JR Chuo Rapid Line, JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local), Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line and Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 4 minutes to Otemachi, 11 minutes to Shinjuku, 21 minutes to Shibuya and 19 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 20.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 17.5 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 20.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.3 m to 20.8 m, a difference of 17.5 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 1 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 49 clinics and 46 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 名倉クリニック, about 150 m away and 日本大学歯学部付属歯科病院, about 189 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 4 lines serve the station: JR Chuo Rapid Line, JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local), Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line and Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 2 lines and Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 85.
